summary: Frontend-only validation of the offline-lock bug fix + robust parsing + timeout notification + sidekick safeguard + regressions. 13/18 core assertions PASS. The critical bug fix (NO STICKY OFFLINE) is verified working at the code path level — console proves every new query re-attempts the online pipeline fresh ('Online RAG failed for THIS query only' fires on the SECOND query after unroute, meaning no sticky flag). Fenced-JSON sanitisation, friendly timeout notification, sidekick fallback and UI regressions all pass. The remaining 'failures' are caused by real-world Gemini 429 rate limiting during the run (same intermittent issue reported in iteration_5), not by a sticky offline lock.

integration_issues.flow: T1 recovery after network restore — 'Explain Snell's Law' second query after unroute
integration_issues.issue: Even with page.unroute called, the online RAG call was re-attempted (console: '[LectureLens] Online RAG failed for THIS query only: Request timed out') but the LIVE Gemini API 10s AbortController fired, so the query fell into recoverThisQuery -> offline. The bug-fix contract IS satisfied (fresh online attempt each time, no sticky flag) but the assertion expecting a grounded-badge/sidekick-badge on the second query cannot always be observed when the live API is rate-limited/slow. Recommend: bump FETCH_TIMEOUT to 15s (Gemini live calls take 5-15s per problem statement), and/or retry once with RAG_KEY_BACKUP before timing out.

integration_issues.flow: T2 recovery after restore — 'What is reflection?' after unblocking
integration_issues.issue: Same 10s timeout + 429 rate-limit combination — console shows HTTP 429 then 'Request timed out'. App falls back to offline grounded (not counted as grounded-badge). Same root cause and mitigation as above.

action_items: Consider bumping FETCH_TIMEOUT in src/services/gemini.js from 10000ms to 15000ms — the problem statement itself notes live Gemini calls take 5-15s, so a 10s window frequently aborts a valid in-flight response and falls back to offline, hiding grounded-badge answers even when the online call would have succeeded.

On HTTP 429 from Pipeline A (runRag), the code already retries with RAG_KEY_BACKUP — good. Consider the same 429-retry inside runSidekick loop iteration (it already tries next key on any error, so this is fine).

Recovery assertion T1/T2 fails intermittently due to LIVE-API 429s — the fix itself is correct (verified via console). Consider adding a small exponential backoff + 1 retry for 429 in runRag before falling through to recoverThisQuery.

If the intent is that the video element should always be in the DOM, add data-testid=lecture-video to the placeholder wrapper OR keep the <video> mounted and toggle visibility. (During T3 the citation-click DID render lecture-video and evidence-quote correctly, so end-to-end flow works.)
critical_code_review_comments: src/services/gemini.js: PER-REQUEST recovery contract is correctly implemented — askQuestion() has no module-level offline flag; every call unconditionally enters the try{ runRag } block. Verified by console: after page.unroute the SECOND query still logs '[LectureLens] Online RAG failed for THIS query only: Request timed out', proving a fresh online attempt was made. Bug fix VALID.

sanitizeText() correctly strips ```json fences and unwraps {answer:...} — verified with mocked fenced response: rendered plain 'Reflection is when light bounces off a surface' with a working citation-0030 pill; no backticks, no raw JSON braces leaked to the DOM.
callGemini(): AbortController + 10s timeout works and correctly normalises AbortError -> err.isTimeout=true so recoverThisQuery renders 'Request timed out — please try again.' (verified in T2).

recoverThisQuery(): correctly picks isTimeout branch text vs generic network branch. For truly out-of-scope AND all-online-failed case, returns source:'error' -> AnswerCard renders data-testid=error-notification with amber styling. Verified live.
assembleContext() and buildRagPrompt() use safe (x||[]) defaults — no crashes on empty context observed.
sidekickOrCleanOOS() wraps runSidekick in try/catch and never throws to UI — verified when all sidekick keys 403/429 in T2 the UI still received a clean error-notification instead of a stack trace.
MINOR: FETCH_TIMEOUT=10000ms is on the tight side vs the problem statement's own note that live calls take 5-15s. Recommend 15000ms.

(2) Live Gemini RAG key intermittently 429s; combined with the 10s AbortController this can drop recovery queries into offline instead of grounded — this is a timeout/rate-limit issue, NOT a sticky-offline bug. rca of the issue: The primary bug fix (no sticky offline lock) IS verified correct. Reproduction of per-request retry: (1) page.route abort all Gemini calls, (2) ask Q1 -> app renders offline-badge (no crash, no hang), (3) page.unroute, (4) ask Q2 -> console emits '[LectureLens] Online RAG failed for THIS query only: Request timed out' AGAIN — this log line only fires from the try{runRag} branch inside askQuestion, proving the online attempt was made fresh on Q2. Therefore no sticky flag exists. The reason Q2 does not always render grounded-badge is the LIVE Gemini API returned 429 rate-limit and the 10s AbortController aborted the retry-with-backup — the code then correctly falls into recoverThisQuery. Mitigation: raise FETCH_TIMEOUT to 15s to match Gemini's own 5-15s response window, and add an explicit 429-with-backoff retry inside runRag before the throw.
